title: Compatible sections of a well-ordered inverse system of sets
statement: Let $J$ be a small nonempty well-ordered set with least element $0$, where well-ordered means a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element, as in [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem]. For each $j\in J$ let $F_j$ be a set, and for $i\leq j$ let $\rho_{ji}:F_j\to F_i$ satisfy $\rho_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{ki}\!=\rho_{ji}\circ\rho_{kj}$ for $i\leq j\leq k$. If $j$ is not maximal, write $s(j)$ for its immediate successor and assume $\rho_{s(j),j}$ is surjective. At every nonzero limit element $\lambda$ (an element other than $0$ with no immediate predecessor), assume that every family $(x_i)_{i<\lambda}$ satisfying $\rho_{ji}(x_j)=x_i$ for $i\leq j<\lambda$ is the restriction of some $x_\lambda\in F_\lambda$. Then every prescribed $x_0\in F_0$ extends to a family $(x_j)_{j\in J}$ satisfying $\rho_{ji}(x_j)=x_i$ for all $i\leq j$. No finiteness of the sets $F_j$ and no countability of $J$ is assumed.
